titulo: Café and food: «queria», numbers to 100, prices in reais: Ordering with «queria»

aula.titulo: Café and food: «queria», numbers to 100, prices in reais
aula.objetivo: Order a coffee and something to eat politely with «queria», count from 20 to 100, understand prices in reais and ask how much it is.

itens.pt: I would like (polite way to ask for something)
how can I help you? (what a shop assistant says)
bakery (also a café and small shop)

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: to ask for something in a café, a shop or a restaurant, Brazilians say «queria» + the thing: «Queria um café, por favor.» It means «I would like a coffee, please». It is polite and natural. You can add «eu» («Eu queria…»), but you do not need to. STEP 2: «queria» comes from the verb «querer» (to want). The full verb is lesson 13; for now learn «queria» as a ready-made phrase for ordering. The plain «quero» (I want) is correct, but it sounds more direct, so «queria» is the safer choice with strangers. STEP 3: the thing you ask for needs «um» or «uma» (or a number), and it must agree with the noun: «um café» (masculine), «uma água» (feminine), «um suco», «uma xícara de café». STEP 4: «de» joins a container or a type to its content: «um copo de água», «uma xícara de café», «suco de laranja», «pão de queijo». English often has no word here, but Portuguese always needs «de». STEP 5: the person serving you may ask «Pois não?» (how can I help you?), «Mais alguma coisa?» (anything else?) and «É pra comer aqui ou pra levar?» (is it to eat here or to take away?). You can answer «É só isso, obrigado» (that is all, thanks) and ask for «a conta, por favor». STEP 6: in the morning, Brazilians have «café da manhã» (breakfast), often in a padaria: coffee, bread with butter, cheese bread, juice, fruit.
blocos.comparacao: In English you say «Can I have…?» or «I'd like…». Portuguese «queria» is the same idea as «I'd like». English «a glass of water» needs «of», and so does Portuguese «um copo de água». Do not say «um copo água».

tabela.you_say: Queria um copo de suco de laranja.
tabela.meaning: I'd like a glass of orange juice.

erros.motivo: «Café» is masculine: «um café». Only «a água» and «a laranja» are feminine here.
A container is joined to its content with «de».
The name of the roll has «de»: «pão de queijo».
In «que» and «qui» the «u» is silent: «queria» starts with a «k» sound.

blocos.enunciado: Order out loud, as if you were at a padaria: a «café com leite», a «pão de queijo» and a «água». Start with «Bom dia!» and finish with «A conta, por favor.»
Greet an imaginary person with the right «bom dia / boa tarde / boa noite», say «tudo bem» and answer with «e você?». Then say with «eu sou» your name and with «eu tenho» your age (numbers 0 to 20).
